chapter: Los Angeles, Central Avenue and the Apex
title: Opening of the Apex Club and Curtis Moseby
summary: The Apex nightclub opened shortly after the Dunbar, run by Curtis Moseby, whose band Royal joined and where he first met Duke Ellington.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So there was a ballroom next door to the Clark and then what did -- and the Dunbar -- at what point did the Apex Club ... ? Downstairs in the Dunbar there was a lounge, wasn't there? (inaudible)?

The Apex was in a different building altogether. It was about 50 yards from the Dunbar Hotel, North of the Somerville Hotel in a building that was put up that was mainly office buildings. All upstairs was -- it was a two-story building. It was -- all the upstairs frontage was office buildings and downstairs they had a half a dozen storefronts and the Apex, which was a nightclub, was built in.
It opened approximately a year or so after

the Dunbar Hotel opened, which opened in '26, the Dunbar opened, I believe, or thereabouts. The Apex opened a little bit after that. The Apex was run by a fellow by the name of Curtis Moseby (PHONETIC) who at that time had a band which I joined for my first nightclub job as a regular. That's where I first met Duke Ellington when he came through, at the Apex.
